description: Two VCAs with different architectures, running side by side or one into the other

params.text: Adds a DC offset to the signal at the first channel's input, negative anticlockwise and positive clockwise
Scales the first channel's input, inverting it anticlockwise and passing it clockwise
Sets the second channel's response curve, linear anticlockwise and exponential clockwise, which also widens the gain available above the fader's unity point
Sets the level of the second channel, unity gain about two thirds up; with a cable in the CV input the fader attenuates that voltage instead
Parallel sums the first channel into the second channel's output while the first channel's own output is unpatched; Series normals the first channel's output into the second channel's input

inputs.text: The signal into the first channel, which is multiplied by whatever reaches the other side of that channel
The other side of the first channel's four quadrant multiplier; unpatched it holds a +5V reference, so the channel works as a bias and attenuverter
Controls the level of the second channel; negative voltage is cropped to 0V, and unpatched the jack holds a +5V reference
The signal into the second channel

outputs.text: The first channel's output; patching it breaks the internal routing into the second channel
The second channel's output, which also carries the first channel when the routing switch is set to Parallel
